distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 109.39 +/- 0.27 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 9.142 +/- 0.023 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 107.8023 +/- 0.1838 mas (same row, RUWE 1.34), 586.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.919 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.936 +/- 0.025 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 0.919 +/- 0.025 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 639,348 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.037 +/- 0.042 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.037 +/- 0.042 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5776 +/- 81 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5776 +/- 81 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 20630: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5776 +/- 81 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
